note: config_readonly has no admin UI, no configure route, no permissions, no Drush commands, no plugins and no config object of its own. All of its state lives in settings.php: $settings['config_readonly'] (the master switch) and $settings['config_readonly_whitelist_patterns'] (an exemption list surfaced through hook_config_readonly_whitelist_patterns()). The module unconditionally swaps core's config.storage service for Drupal\config_readonly\Config\ConfigReadonlyStorage via ConfigReadonlyServiceProvider::alter(); that storage throws ConfigReadonlyStorageException from write/delete/rename/deleteAll unless the lock is off, a ConfigImporter run holds the config_importer lock, the route is system.db_update, or the config name matches a whitelist pattern. A second guard (config_readonly_form_alter + ReadOnlyFormSubscriber, priority 200) disables submit buttons on ConfigFormBase / ConfigEntityListBuilder / ConfigTranslationFormBase / config-entity forms and on config_single_import_form, system_modules, system_modules_uninstall and user_admin_permissions. Medium and hard cases are grounded in that real settings.php state and in the live module handler's hook aggregation; they deliberately never activate the lock on this shared site (the lock-state case installs a conditional block that stays OFF), so no case can leave the site write-protected.

evals.prompt: I installed and enabled the Drupal contrib module config_readonly on a site, but I can still save every configuration form. Why does enabling the module alone not lock anything, and exactly what do I have to do to make the active configuration store read-only?
evals.expected_output: config_readonly has no admin UI and no configure route. The lock is a site setting: add $settings['config_readonly'] = TRUE; to settings.php (often wrapped in an environment conditional). Until that setting is truthy, both guards (ConfigReadonlyStorage::checkLock() and config_readonly_form_alter()) return early. /admin/reports/status shows 'Config is writable — The Config Read-only module is enabled but not active' in that state.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site locked down with config_readonly I still need the maintenance-mode setting and every view to stay editable. What are the two supported ways to exempt specific configuration from the lock, and what wildcard syntax do the exemption patterns support?
evals.expected_output: Either set $settings['config_readonly_whitelist_patterns'] = ['system.maintenance', 'views.view.*']; in settings.php (config_readonly implements hook_config_readonly_whitelist_patterns() to return that setting) or implement hook_config_readonly_whitelist_patterns() in your own module and return the same kind of array. Patterns are preg_quote'd with '*' turned into '.*' and anchored with ^...$, so '*' is the only wildcard and the pattern must match the whole config name.

evals.prompt: With config_readonly active on a Drupal 11 production site, does `drush config:import` still work, and does update.php still work? Explain the mechanism in ConfigReadonlyStorage that lets those through while ordinary config saves throw an exception. Name the exception class.
evals.expected_output: Yes to both. ConfigReadonlyStorage::checkLock() only throws Drupal\config_readonly\Exception\ConfigReadonlyStorageException when Settings::get('config_readonly') is truthy AND $this->lock->lockMayBeAvailable(ConfigImporter::LOCK_NAME) is TRUE — during a config import the importer holds the 'config_importer' lock so the check returns early. It also returns early when the current request's route is system.db_update (update.php). Otherwise write(), delete(), rename() and deleteAll() throw.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has config_readonly installed and a whitelist of configuration that is exempt from the read-only lock. Inspect the running site and list every whitelist pattern that is currently in effect.
evals.expected_output: Three patterns are in effect: system.maintenance, mymodule.editable_settings and views.view.cr_eval_*. They come from $settings['config_readonly_whitelist_patterns'] in settings.php, which config_readonly returns from its own hook_config_readonly_whitelist_patterns() implementation; the aggregated list is readable with drush php:eval 'print_r(\Drupal::moduleHandler()->invokeAll("config_readonly_whitelist_patterns"));'.

evals.prompt: settings.php on this Drupal site contains a $settings['config_readonly'] assignment, and the config_readonly module is enabled. Inspect the RUNNING site and tell me whether the configuration active store is actually locked right now — and say which class the config.storage service currently resolves to.
evals.expected_output: The store is NOT locked. The settings.php assignment is inside `if (getenv('CR_EVAL_LOCK') === '1')` and that variable is not set, so Settings::get('config_readonly') returns NULL and both guards return early — the status report says 'Config is writable / The Config Read-only module is enabled but not active'. The config.storage service is nevertheless always Drupal\config_readonly\Config\ConfigReadonlyStorage, because ConfigReadonlyServiceProvider::alter() swaps the class unconditionally.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, config_readonly is installed. Using the module's settings.php whitelist mechanism, make exactly two things exempt from the read-only lock: the config object `system.maintenance`, and every Views config entity (all `views.view.*` objects). Do not whitelist anything else and do not turn the lock itself on. Apply the change to the live site so the running site reports both exemptions.
evals.expected_output: Add to web/sites/default/settings.php: $settings['config_readonly_whitelist_patterns'] = ['system.maintenance', 'views.view.*'];  config_readonly's own hook_config_readonly_whitelist_patterns() returns that setting, so \Drupal::moduleHandler()->invokeAll('config_readonly_whitelist_patterns') then yields both patterns, and ConfigReadonlyWhitelistTrait::matchesWhitelistPattern() (preg_quote + '*'→'.*', anchored ^...$) matches system.maintenance, views.view.frontpage and views.view.content but not system.site.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, config_readonly is installed. Create and enable a custom module with the machine name `cr_eval_whitelist` at web/modules/custom/cr_eval_whitelist that supplies the config_readonly exemption pattern `cr_eval.settings` through the module hook config_readonly invites — not through settings.php. Leave settings.php untouched.
evals.expected_output: web/modules/custom/cr_eval_whitelist/cr_eval_whitelist.info.yml (type: module, core_version_requirement, dependency on config_readonly) plus cr_eval_whitelist.module implementing function cr_eval_whitelist_config_readonly_whitelist_patterns() { return ['cr_eval.settings']; }, then `drush en cr_eval_whitelist -y`. Afterwards \Drupal::moduleHandler()->invokeAllWith('config_readonly_whitelist_patterns', ...) lists cr_eval_whitelist as an implementor and invokeAll() contains 'cr_eval.settings', while Settings::get('config_readonly_whitelist_patterns') does not.
